system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
**Buyer-side review:** The Seller’s “STANDARD”, “FINAL” and alleged prior-agreement labels are not evidence of Buyer approval. Review all positions against the AUD 24 million, debt-free/cash-free acquisition baseline. The numerical positions below are proposed negotiation asks, not established market requirements. Underlying DD documents and the complete SPA have not been supplied.

| Issue | Seller’s position | What the Buyer should want | Recommendation — one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General warranty liability capped at **20% / AUD 4.8m**. | A higher general cap, with separate treatment for fundamental warranties, tax, specific indemnities and fraud. | **Counter at 50% / AUD 12m**, subject to diligence and recovery security — the appropriate cap should reflect actual exposure, not the Seller’s unsupported market assertion. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | Claims must exceed **AUD 25,000** individually and **AUD 250,000** collectively; only the excess over the basket is recoverable. | Lower thresholds, a tipping basket, aggregation of related claims, and exclusions for protected categories. | **Propose AUD 10,000 de minimis and AUD 100,000 tipping basket**, excluding fundamental, tax and specific-indemnity claims — the current combination leaves meaningful losses with the Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | General claims notified within **18 months**; limitations extend to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | At least **24 months** for general warranties; separate periods for other categories and preservation of claims notified in time. | **Seek 24 months and reject automatic cross-application**, checking any proceedings deadline — the Buyer needs sufficient time to discover and investigate breaches through reporting cycles. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties share the general cap and time limit. | Separate protection for capacity, ownership, valid issuance and unencumbered transfer of all shares; no basket/de minimis, a **100% price cap**, and materially longer survival. | **Require a standalone fundamental regime**, seeking the longest appropriate enforceable period — a defect in ownership or authority threatens the acquisition itself. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance apply to all Claims; no express fraud carve-out is identified. | An overriding carve-out for fraud and fraudulent concealment from caps, thresholds, contractual time bars, disclosure/knowledge defences and remedy restrictions; preserve non-excludable rights. | **Insist on an express, overriding carve-out**, with appropriate attribution to the Seller — misconduct must not receive contractual protection through broad limitation language. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of the data room, accounts, registers and public records, plus specific disclosures. | Only fair disclosure with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of an exception, mapped to relevant warranties; a fixed, archived disclosure record. | **Reject blanket/deemed disclosure and narrow permitted exceptions**, ensuring disclosure does not qualify specific indemnities unless expressly agreed — document availability alone should not transfer unidentified risks. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | Bars claims for Buyer/adviser knowledge, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records. | Delete the qualifier; alternatively restrict it to actual conscious knowledge of named Buyer individuals at signing, without constructive or imputed adviser knowledge. | **Reject the discoverability standard**, with protected categories expressly excluded from any compromise — the Seller should not escape warranties because diligence could theoretically have uncovered a problem. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent, despite missing final consent and evidence of associated conditions. | A Buyer-waivable completion condition requiring effective consent and satisfaction of clause 11.3 conditions, without materially adverse changes. | **Make satisfactory consent and condition fulfilment a completion gate**, supported by evidence — Bluefen represents approximately 30% of FY26 revenue, so a consent document alone may be inadequate. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** outstanding; security release follows Completion. | Repayment through an agreed completion funds flow, lender payout confirmation and effective release of security and relevant guarantees at Completion. | **Require a simultaneous lender-controlled discharge arrangement**, with debt deducted under the agreed price mechanics and no double counting — the Buyer must not pay a debt-free price while inheriting secured debt. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | **AUD 420,000** conditional completion bonuses omitted from funds flow; Seller calls them its matter; on-cost treatment unspecified. | Establish the liability, payment timing, conditions and payroll tax/superannuation/other on-costs; allocate Seller transaction-related liabilities expressly. | **Include applicable bonuses and on-costs as Seller-funded payments or debt-like deductions, backed by protection for unpaid amounts**, without duplication — omission could leave the acquired company funding the Seller’s transaction costs. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment; transfer depends on cleared payment of all SOW3 fees; **AUD 180,000** remains recorded as open. | Verified settlement and effective vesting/confirmatory assignment of necessary IP, plus protection for ownership defects and resulting claims, remediation and business losses. | **Require payment evidence and IP cure before Completion, plus a broader standalone indemnity** — payment-only cover does not ensure the company owns or can exploit the materials. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Described as preliminary and unlikely material; possible export of approximately **1,240 records**, with access, scope and notification unresolved. | Prompt forensic investigation, containment, preservation of evidence and advice on applicable notification duties; specific protection for pre-Completion exposure. | **Require investigation milestones, compliant remediation and a tailored indemnity/security; assess whether unresolved severity warrants a completion condition** — uncertainty is not evidence of immateriality, but neither is this yet a confirmed notifiable breach. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three **AUD 110,000** renewals treated as ordinary-course operating costs. | Assess the **AUD 330,000 aggregate** commitment, timing, scope, termination rights, accrual and consistency with ordinary course and agreed covenants. | **Review DD-008 and DD-011 together before allocating cost**, with consent controls for new commitments — neither ordinary-course status nor debt-like treatment is established by the supplied facts. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | General limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance apply to all Claims unless expressly displaced. | Explicitly separate general warranties, fundamentals, tax, specific indemnities, price adjustments, debt/payment obligations and covenants; preserve fraud and non-excludable remedies. | **Draft a category-by-category limitations matrix with clear precedence rules** — otherwise catch-all drafting can silently neutralise negotiated protections. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | Relies on DD-012’s share register showing Harbourglass owns 100%. | Independent reconciliation of issued capital, ownership history, constitution, certificates/transfers, options and other equity rights, encumbrances and transfer restrictions. | **Verify title and require effective completion transfers, approvals and releases, backed by fundamental warranties** — the register is important evidence, not complete assurance of unencumbered ownership. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Tax and IP warranties considered settled under the general regime. | Separate tax warranties and a pre-Completion tax indemnity with appropriate assessment-period survival; substantive IP ownership, licensing, infringement and software diligence protections. | **Reopen both packages expressly**, with tailored caps, exclusions and survival, coordinating Ironquay without double recovery — historical tax and core-IP risks should not default into a short, broadly qualified general warranty regime. |
=== END ADVICE ===
